name: Product Owner (PrOw)
one_liner: Single voice of the stakeholders; owns and prioritises the Work Items List.
purpose: The Product Owner (PrOw) represents mainly client and end-user concerns and develops a deep understanding of stakeholder needs, which allows the role to capture and set priorities for the Work Items. The PrOw is the 'single voice of the stakeholders' inside the Agile Project Core Team (A-PCT) and should ideally sit in the same physical environment as the rest of the team. With PM²-Agile the PrOw also becomes the permanent point of contact between the requester and provider organisations.

fields.what: Prioritises the Work Items List to be addressed by the A-PCT, aligned with feedback from stakeholders and from the team.
fields.who: Determines priority together with the Business Manager
fields.pollux: Curie decides Release 1 ships read-only exposure by member state, nothing more.

fields.what: Answers the team's domain-related questions or ensures an open channel to the relevant stakeholders for clarification.
fields.pollux: Settles whether a maturity bucket follows the accounts or the lending platform.

fields.what: Facilitates requirements gathering and modelling sessions, including Design Block workshops with the team.
fields.pollux: Runs the workshop where Risk, the Board and Finance state incompatible report needs.

fields.what: Ensures the stakeholder community is represented; the PrOw is the single voice of the stakeholders in the team.
fields.pollux: Represents Risk, Finance and the Board inside a team that meets none of them daily.

fields.what: Facilitates the presentation of the project's intermediate outputs to the stakeholder community.
fields.who: ATeMs may deliver or delegate the demo
fields.pollux: Demonstrates the reconciliation panel to national authorities before Release 2 closes.

fields.what: Ensures stakeholders understand the benefits of the agile approach the A-PCT is following.
fields.pollux: Explains to Medici why a fixed scope was never available for POLLUX.

fields.what: Should ideally work in the same physical environment as the rest of the Agile Project Core Team.
fields.pollux: Curie sits with the team in Kirchberg rather than in Reporting.

fields.what: Proposes the Iteration Goal and is accountable for the goal agreed with the Agile Project Core Team.
fields.who: ATeMs are Responsible for Iteration Planning itself
fields.pollux: Sets the goal for iteration 1, starting 08 Jan 2029.

fields.f: Accepts or rejects in the Review
fields.what: Provides feedback on demonstrated items, accepting or rejecting them according to the acceptance criteria.
fields.who: ATeMs run the ceremony; BM and BIG are consulted
fields.pollux: Rejects a story that meets acceptance criteria but fails the Definition of Done.

fields.what: Becomes the permanent contact between requester and provider organisations, aligning scope and time-frame expectations.
fields.pollux: Absorbs the quarterly requirement churn that used to reach the PM.

fields.what: Acts as liaison between the User Representatives and the provider organisation through regular refinement sessions.
fields.pollux: Runs refinement with the analysts who assembled the eleven spreadsheets.

fields.what: Ensures User Representatives participate actively in the Iteration Review to validate the team's iteration output.
fields.pollux: Brings a Risk analyst to review the scenario overlay in Release 3.

fields.what: Must be empowered by the Business Manager to take day-to-day decisions so the team never waits for a decision.
fields.pollux: Hopper empowers Curie; without it POLLUX stalls every fortnight.

fields.what: Must be aligned with the Business Manager and the BIG so the Work Items List reflects business strategy and vision.
fields.pollux: Conflict 3 — Curie and Hopper disagree over Release 2 content.

fields.what: Prioritises enabler items alongside business items; the Architecture Owner helps find the right balance.
fields.pollux: Accepts Einstein's enabler stories into Release 1 instead of three enabler iterations.

fields.f: Informed, not central, in the team's own ceremonies
fields.what: Is informed of Daily Stand-up and Retrospective outcomes only if necessary; those belong to the ATeMs.
fields.pollux: Curie skips the stand-up; the team's process is Lovelace's ground.

traps: PrOw is not the Business Manager; the BM empowers and aligns but does not prioritise.
PrOw is Responsible for the Work Items List; the Project Manager is Accountable.
PrOw supports Iteration Planning — the ATeMs are Responsible for running it.
Domain experts may join, but the PrOw remains the single voice of the stakeholders.
PrOw does not facilitate ceremonies; the Team Coordinator does.
